infra-bot: ALERT — Dedicated pool 'nova-enterprise' GPU saturation for tenant Altamira (tenant-id: alt-9876). GPU util 99%, queue length 14, 503s of queued requests. Paging @Aria (oncall).
Aria (oncall): I'm on it. Joining call informally.
Ravi (eng-runtime): I see KV cache pressure + long tail. Per-GPU queued tokens spiking. Logs:
```
[alt-9876] assign_task failed: no free GPU slots
queue_length=14 gpu_util=99.1% running_jobs=48
```
Lena (sre): Confirming: host-level metrics show all GPUs at 99% across the pool. Any recent deploys? None in last 2h.
Rowan (cs): I'm pinging Altamira POC Armitage now — will advise customer-facing mitigation.
Armitage (Altamira POC): We just kicked off a large nightly batch by mistake, that's likely the cause. Can we throttle it? It's critical but they can delay non-urgent jobs.
Ravi (eng-runtime): Two options: (A) enable 30m emergency burst to allow Altamira extra capacity (we have reserved burst credits), or (B) evict best-effort tenants to free GPUs. Eviction may affect other customers.
ops-kai: @Ravi confirm burst policy — ops lead gives emergency approval for burst if customer confirms impact is service-affecting.
Rowan (cs): Customer confirms the batch can be limited to 25% concurrency for next 45m.
Ravi (eng-runtime): I'll patch tenant throttle immediately and request burst as safety net.
Ravi (eng-runtime): Command run:
```
infractl tenant throttle --tenant alt-9876 --concurrency 25% --scope pool:nova-enterprise
infractl pool burst-request --pool nova-enterprise --tenant alt-9876 --duration 45m --reason "emergency tenant burst per CS" --approver ops-kai
```
infra-bot: BURST_REQUEST received (id=br-7621). Awaiting ops-kai approval.
ops-kai: Approved. Executing burst now.
infra-bot: BURST_APPROVED br-7621 — provisioning +2 GPUs to nova-enterprise. Expected attach time ~90s.

Rowan (cs): Notified customer — Altamira will reduce concurrency and monitor. They said thanks.
Ravi (eng-runtime): Followups: 1) Schedule autoscale policy update for this pool (lower aggressiveness for single-tenant spikes). 2) Postmortem to review tenant throttling knobs and user safeguards.
Aria (oncall): Handing off to night oncall @Lena in 20m. I'll update incident channel with runbook actions and add customer timeline.
